front.title: ai-systems.txt: A Well-Known File for Declaring AI Systems and Their Measured Capabilities

abstract.t: This document defines "ai-systems.txt", a plain-text file that an organisation that builds or deploys artificial intelligence (AI) systems publishes at a well-known location on its own domain. The file declares, in machine-readable and human-readable form, which AI systems the organisation has released, what their measured capabilities are, who measured them, under what conditions, and where the evidence lives. Every capability claim carries a provenance tier (ATTESTED, MEASURED, or DECLARED); anything absent from a valid, unexpired file is UNDECLARED by definition. The file is signed and expiring, so claims are attributable, timestamped, and falsifiable. robots.txt tells machines what they may take from a publisher; ai- systems.txt is the reverse: it tells anyone what a maker has built, in a form designed to be checked rather than believed.
